title: "Save with me" challenge hooks are leading FinTok
why_it_works: Savings-challenge and contrarian one-liner hooks are outperforming straight advice on TikTok right now. Longer-form (1-3 min) is beating 15-second clips on watch time and reach because the algorithm rewards completion rate over polish.
how_to_film: Phone in hand, natural light, no script on paper. Say the number in the first 3 seconds: "I put $300 a month into my CPF SA, here's what happened." Walk through the real math on screen (write it on paper or a notes app) for 60-90 seconds. Don't cut away from your face for more than a beat.

title: Document (PDF carousel) posts are LinkedIn's top-engagement format
why_it_works: Document posts hit roughly 6.6% engagement, the highest of any LinkedIn format, ahead of native video at 5.6%. LinkedIn's 2026 algorithm ranks on dwell time, and a slide deck keeps a reader on the post far longer than a text wall.
how_to_film: No camera needed. Take one topic (e.g. "3 CPF moves before you turn 35") and break it into 5-6 slides, one idea per slide, big text, your face only on the first and last slide. Build it in Canva or Keynote, export as PDF, upload as a LinkedIn document post.

title: A direct question at the end drives 77% more comments
why_it_works: Posts that end with a direct question see about 77% more comments than average, and adding an explicit "comment below" CTA pushes that higher still. Comments in the first 48 hours drive roughly half of a post's total distribution.
how_to_film: Not a video trend, a writing one: end every LinkedIn post with one specific question tied to the topic, not "thoughts?". E.g. after a CPF post: "Did you top up your SA before 35, or are you waiting? Tell me why."

title: Infographic Reels get saved 3x more than talking-head finance content
why_it_works: Saves are Instagram's strongest distribution signal for finance content specifically. Animated pie-chart breakdowns and compounding-interest visuals with real dollar amounts get bookmarked to reread later, which talking-head videos rarely do.
how_to_film: Build a simple animated or static breakdown (Canva has templates) showing one real number arc: e.g. "$500/month into SRS from age 30 vs 40" with the end balances shown big. Caption should restate the numbers so it's save-worthy even muted.

title: A specific dollar figure outperforms vague advice on every platform
why_it_works: "Save more" gets scrolled past; "$500/month into a Roth IRA" gets saved. This holds across TikTok, Reels, and LinkedIn in 2026 research - specificity is the single biggest lever separating high- and low-performing finance content.
how_to_film: Before filming anything, force yourself to pick one real number: an amount, a percentage, an age, a timeframe. Write it into your hook line. If your hook could apply to any advisor's content, it's too vague - make it about a specific, generic-yet-real client scenario.
source_label: FlowCast - Instagram Reels Hooks That Work in 2026

title: Myth-busting is the highest-leverage template across all platforms
why_it_works: "[Common belief] is wrong, here's why" performs identically well on TikTok, Reels, and LinkedIn because it opens a curiosity gap immediately and challenges an assumption the viewer already holds - the format doesn't need to change per platform, only the length.
how_to_film: Open with the myth stated as fact, pause half a second, then "...actually not true." Then explain in under 45 seconds with one real example. Works as a 30-sec TikTok, a 3-slide LinkedIn carousel, or an IG Reel with the myth as on-screen text.
source_label: Insurance Snapshot for GHL - 2026 Organic Growth Playbook

title: Behind-the-firm content is under-used and over-performs
why_it_works: Showing your actual process - how a client review works, who's on your team, what happens after someone signs up - performs well precisely because most advisors skip it in favour of polished promotional content. Familiarity builds trust faster than credentials do.
how_to_film: Film 20-30 seconds of something ordinary: prepping for a client meeting, your notes system, your desk at the end of the day. No script, just narrate what you're doing and why it matters to a client watching.
source_label: Insurance Snapshot for GHL - 2026 Organic Growth Playbook

title: Life-event trigger content converts better than generic education
why_it_works: "Just had a baby? Review these 3 coverages" outperforms generic "here's why insurance matters" content because it targets a reader at the exact moment they're likely to act, not a hypothetical future self.
how_to_film: Pick one life event common in your client base (new baby, first HDB, first job, marriage) and film a 3-frame story or 30-sec Reel: what changes, what to review, one action to take this week. Repeat this template across different life events as a recurring series.
source_label: Insurance Snapshot for GHL - 2026 Organic Growth Playbook

title: Comic-style visual breakdowns are the Singapore reference format
why_it_works: The Woke Salaryman built its audience on turning dense local topics (CPF, HDB, insurance) into simple comic-style visual breakdowns instead of talking-head explainers - a format that's inherently team-generic and easy for any FC to adapt without needing to be the on-camera personality.
how_to_film: Doesn't require drawing skill - use a simple template (stick figures, icons, or Canva illustration packs) to show a before/after or a decision tree for one SG-specific topic. Keep the visual metaphor simple enough to screenshot and understand without sound.
source_label: With Content - The Woke Salaryman Content Strategy

title: One recording, three formats - the efficient way to keep up with all three platforms
why_it_works: Advisors who stay consistent don't film three separate pieces of content. Record one solid explainer, then repurpose: the raw cut goes to TikTok/Reels, the strongest 3-5 points become a LinkedIn document carousel, and the best 15 seconds becomes a Reels teaser linking back.
how_to_film: Record a single 60-90 second phone video on a topic you already explain to clients weekly. Immediately after: (1) post the raw cut to TikTok, (2) turn your talking points into a slide carousel for LinkedIn, (3) clip the strongest line as a 15-sec IG teaser.
source_label: The Advisor Coach - Video Marketing for Financial Advisors
